note: Local-first detection patterns. Bundled with the extension and refreshed from jikida.io/extension/patterns.json (cached 24h). v2 adds malware/skimmer JS, runtime-config disclosure, and more secret families. Each secret pattern is scoped so intentionally-public client keys are labelled correctly.

secrets.label: AWS access key ID
secrets.note: An AWS access key ID in client code almost always means the matching secret key is nearby or was committed. Rotate immediately.

secrets.label: Google API key
secrets.note: Google Maps/JS keys are meant to be public. Severity depends on restrictions: an UNRESTRICTED key (no HTTP-referrer / API limits) can be abused and billed to you. We flag it as an exposure to verify, not a confirmed leak.

secrets.label: Firebase web config
secrets.note: Firebase web config is public by design. Real risk is weak Firestore/Storage security rules — check whether data is readable without auth.

secrets.label: Supabase project URL
secrets.note: The Supabase URL + anon key are public by design. The risk is misconfigured Row Level Security — verify whether tables are readable with only the anon key.

secrets.label: Supabase SERVICE ROLE key (should never be in the browser)
secrets.note: The service_role JWT bypasses Row Level Security. It must NEVER reach the browser. If present, treat every row as fully exposed.

secrets.label: Stripe publishable key
secrets.note: Publishable keys are meant for the client. No action needed.

secrets.label: JSON Web Token
secrets.note: A JWT in client code is often the user's own session token (normal). Flagged as info unless it decodes to a privileged/service role.

secrets.label: Hard-coded secret/password assignment
secrets.note: Heuristic: a key/secret assigned a literal string in client JS. Needs verification — may be a placeholder or a real credential.

secrets.label: GitHub personal access token
secrets.note: A GitHub PAT grants repo access. Rotate it and move it server-side.

security_headers.name: Strict-Transport-Security
security_headers.why: Without HSTS a first request can be downgraded to HTTP and intercepted.

security_headers.name: Content-Security-Policy
security_headers.why: CSP is the strongest defence against XSS. Missing means injected scripts run freely.

security_headers.name: X-Content-Type-Options
security_headers.why: Stops MIME sniffing that can turn an upload into executable script.

security_headers.name: X-Frame-Options
security_headers.why: Prevents clickjacking by disallowing your page inside a frame (or use CSP frame-ancestors).

security_headers.name: Referrer-Policy
security_headers.why: Controls how much of your URL leaks to other sites in the Referer header.

security_headers.name: Permissions-Policy
security_headers.why: Locks down powerful browser features (camera, geolocation) your app doesn't use.

malware_js.label: Crypto-miner script
malware_js.note: Crypto-mining JavaScript hijacks visitor CPUs. If you didn't add this, the site may be compromised.

malware_js.label: Possible card skimmer
malware_js.note: Code hooking payment fields is a Magecart-style skimmer pattern. Review immediately if you take payments.

malware_js.label: Obfuscated/packed JS payload
malware_js.note: Packed/obfuscated eval payloads are a common malware delivery pattern. Verify the source of this script.

malware_js.label: Cookie exfiltration
malware_js.note: Sending document.cookie to a network endpoint can leak sessions. Confirm this is a legitimate analytics call.
